sources_read.section: a manifest whose only icon was favicon.ico
how `fallbacks` is wired (PrecacheFallbackPlugin) and that navigationPreload is only ever enabled
defaultCache's routes (no document route unless production, and PAGES_CACHE_NAME html)

scope: Icons, the manifest, the worker's navigation strategy, an offline page, and iOS metadata. Out of scope: push, background sync, and the app's own offline data layer (task 016).

acceptance_criteria.text: The manifest is served with 192/512/maskable icons that return 200.
apple-mobile-web-app-capable and an apple-touch-icon are in the served HTML.
The precache holds the shell; an offline navigation renders the app, not a browser error.
verify green; a production build clean; offline navigation of /w and of a deep link both render.

open_questions: Whether the pilot wants the offline page (`/~offline`) surfaced anywhere; it is precached and reachable, but the shell answers navigations.
risks: A service worker is sticky: changes only reach a returning client on the next load, and a stale registration keeps navigation preload on unless the new worker disables it (it does).
Precaching the shell means a deploy's shell HTML updates on the next visit, not instantly.
The maskable icon needs a real Android install to confirm the safe zone.
